To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) blood pressure measurement, hemoglobin tests and transabdominal ultrasound are cornerstone for the diagnosis of gynecologic life-threatening emergencies; (2) standardised questioning about symptoms can be used for triaging patients; (3) the diagnostic accuracy of clinical examination is low and should not be used to rule out gynecologic life threatening emergencies; and (4) the diagnostic accuracy for all other signs or tests is too low to be recommended
the best diagnostic tools for G-PLEs are: blood pressure measurement, transvaginal ultrasonography and haemoglobin tests.

blood pressure measurement and transvagial ultrasound are the cornerstone examinations for the management of gynecological emergencies, while standardised questioning about symptoms may be used for triaging patients.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new diagnostic tools for G-PLEs and their implementation in emergency departments.
the identification of non-invasive tools that can be used for the diagnosis of major G-PLEs.
the development of an integrated system for diagnosis and treatment of patients suffering from gynecological emergencies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a combination of clinical examination and laboratory tests with ultrasound examination would be the best approach in the diagnosis of GPLEs.
transvaginal ultrasonography is the most accurate diagnostic tool for G-PLEs.
transvaginal ultrasonography, with its ability to detect haemoperitoneal fluid, adnexal mass and/or Doppler flow abnormalities, has a major role in the diagnosis of Gynaecological PLEs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a combination of a few non-invasive tests could provide a rapid diagnosis in patients presenting with a G-PLE.
the most common diagnostic tools are transvaginal ultrasonography, medical history, clinical examination and laboratory tests.
a systematic review of the literature on the diagnosis of gynaecological life-threatening emergencies was conducted, which identified 45 studies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the diagnosis of the G-PLEs is based on the use of a combination of non-invasive tools.
there is a need to improve the methodological quality of diagnostic studies in emergency care, in particular in gynaecology.

the diagnosis of Gynaecological PLEs should be based on a combination of clinical examination and laboratory tests, as well as transvaginal ultrasonography, which should be considered a cornerstone examination.
